transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's my hairline, mostly, and... and just the way my face looks. I work as a host at a restaurant, and under those lights there, I just feel like I look really old and strange. 

It's on my mind all the time. The people I work with tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I know what I see, and I just can't seem to get past it.
Because of these worries about your appearance, do you find yourself repeatedly doing things like checking in mirrors, fixing your hair, or trying to hide your face?

Yeah, I do. A lot, actually. Especially right before a shift. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I even take pictures on my phone from different angles to see how bad it looks, and... and I keep combing my hair forward to try and cover it up. 

I just get stuck replaying how the guests are going to see me when they walk in. It gets to the point where I end up running late, or I just get too worked up to even go out to the front of the restaurant.

Aside from worries about your appearance, do you have other repetitive thoughts or habits that you feel compelled to do, such as repeatedly checking locks, excessive cleaning, or arranging things in a specific way?

No, not really. I mean, I make sure the door is locked when I leave the house, like anyone else, but it's not something I get stuck on. I don't have to go back and check it over and over or anything like that. It's really just... just the stuff with my hair and my face that takes up all my time and energy. I don't really have any habits with cleaning or organizing things.
Do you ever think that your perception of your appearance might be exaggerated, or are you completely convinced that your hairline and face look as bad as you think?

I'm not really sure. I mean, I guess because my coworkers tell me they don't see it, part of me wonders if... if maybe I'm making it worse in my head. 

But when I actually look in the mirror, it's just so obvious to me. I see exactly how bad it is. So, most of the time, yeah, I'm completely convinced it looks as awful as I think it does. I just can't see it any other way.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (hairline and face) that is unnoticeable or appears slight to others (dysmorphophobia / body dysmorphic disorder, classified under ICD-10 F45.2 Hypochondriacal disorder). This is accompanied by repetitive compulsive behaviors (repeated mirror checking, taking photos at multiple angles, repeatedly combing hair to conceal the perceived flaw) causing significant functional impairment and distress. General obsessive-compulsive rituals unrelated to appearance are absent, ruling out standard OCD (F42).

Persistent belief that they look old and strange despite reassurance from coworkers

Taking repeated photos on phone from different angles to inspect appearance
Repeatedly combing hair forward to camouflage perceived defects

additional_requirements: Absence of general OCD obsessions or compulsions unrelated to appearance
